jobs.title: Systems Engineering Architect
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Systems Engineering Architect to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the VP, Engineering, the Systems Engineering Architect will lead the design and integration of advanced space satellite architectures. This role requires deep expertise across avionics, power, propulsion, security, computer architecture, communications, and navigation, with a proven ability to architect complex “systems of systems” that enable next-generation orbital mobility, secure communications, and resilient mission operations. As a senior technical leader, you will define technology roadmaps, lead analysis of alternatives, and oversee the integration of multi-domain subsystems into cohesive spacecraft architectures. You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams, government stakeholders, and industry partners to deliver breakthrough satellite capabilities on schedule and within budget. Key Duties and Responsibilities Define and implement spacecraft system architecture roadmaps aligned with mission objectives. Lead Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) to evaluate avionics, power, propulsion, communication, and navigation solutions. Establish technical standards and architectures that support interoperability across platforms. Architect end-to-end satellite solutions spanning avionics, power, propulsion, security, computer systems, communications, and navigation. jobs.title: Test Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Test Software Engineer to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Manager, Systems Integration & Test Engineering the Test Software Engineer will work within a multidisciplinary team to create test software products required to build, integrate, and test space vehicles at both the sub-system and system levels. The Test Software Engineer will develop, execute, and support a comprehensive set of test software applications and tools. The role includes configuration management for all associated applications and tools, regular communication of progress and issues to leadership, and development, integration, and maintenance of test solutions using LabVIEW and NI TestStand to support automated test execution, hardware interfacing, and data management across spacecraft test environments. Key Duties and Responsibilities Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate automated testing best practices into the software development lifecycle Create and maintain automated tests for spacecraft subsystems from functional through performance and stress testing Create and maintain Python libraries and packages to promote modularity and code reuse within the test automation ecosystem Work with responsible engineers to derive test requirements for under-defined systems Generate software test requirements and use requirement management tools Develop and maintain software tools and scripts (primarily Python, with Bash as needed) to optimize workflows

jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE JOB The Supply Chain Compliance Project Manager is a hands-on builder within the Supply Chain Program Development team who designs, documents, and deploys the compliance processes that allow our supply chain to operate in a defense environment. This role requires someone who can take ambiguous regulatory and contractual requirements—FAR/DFARS, ITAR, export controls, and customer flow-downs—and partner with subject matter experts to translate them into clear, executable workflows that withstand internal review, customer scrutiny, and government audit. You'll own complete compliance workstreams from discovery through implementation—conducting stakeholder interviews, mapping current-state processes, identifying gaps and control weaknesses, designing future-state solutions, and leading the deployment and change management efforts required to make them stick. This isn't a policy writing role. You'll work directly with Procurement, Quality, Manufacturing, and Engineering to ensure compliance is embedded into how we actually work, not just how we say we work. The Compliance Project Manager collaborates closely with Program Managers, Supply Chain leadership, Legal, and Contracts to transform regulatory obligations into documented, auditable, and repeatable business processes. You'll build the artifacts that prove compliance—compliance matrices, control documentation, desk guides, training materials, and audit readiness packages. As Deputy Chief Engineer in Discovery, you lead the technical work on concepts nobody has proven, usually several at once. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first. You'll be shipping real fixes in the real codebase. You're just entering the codebase through "this broke on a vehicle" instead of "here's a clean feature spec." Once you've built up cross-subsystem fluency - which this role forces faster than sitting in one subsystem ever would - you move into owning subsystems and roadmap work like anyone else. What you'll actually be doing Take a field-reported anomaly (sensor stopped publishing, mission faulted mid-track, data stream drifted for no obvious reason) and figure out what subsystem it's actually in - not just where it was reported.
